title: Capacity claim concierge allocation plan — Jul 2026
summary: Working allocation worksheet for resolving overlapping dedicated GPU reservation claims across regions and contracts. Focused on a concierge-driven triage and temporary tiling to preserve SLAs while maximizing utilization.
body:
PURPOSE:
- Operational sheet used by Capacity Concierge (infra ops) to resolve overlapping contract claims and produce a near-term allocation schedule for Dedicated customers. Not a final commitment ledger; this feeds into the reservation system after signoff.

ASSUMPTIONS & GROUND RULES:
- Customers have SLA tiers: Bronze / Silver / Gold / Enterprise. Tiebreakers: SLA tier -> committed dollars -> historical sustained usage -> contractual start date.
- Each reservation measured in GPU-slices (1 slice = 1xA100-80GB equivalent). Regions treated independently unless explicit cross-region failover is requested.
- Buffer policy: 10% buffer reserved for burst and failover for Enterprise / Gold; 5% for Silver; 0% for Bronze.
- Utilization projections are 90-day rolling windows. Last 30-day p50/p90 token rates used for demand projection.

COLUMNS (spreadsheet columns exported to this doc):
Contract ID | Customer | SLA Tier | Region | Reserved Slices | Provisional Allocation (slices) | Peak Util% (proj) | Allocation Window | Buffer slice | Notes / conflicts | Action owner

ROWS (current triage snapshot):
C-2026-091 | StellarHealth | Enterprise | us-west1 | 120 | 108 | 76% | 2026-07-15 -> 2026-10-14 | 12 | Overlaps with C-2026-114 in same region; requested hard pin for Q3 marketing surge. Pending proof of burst pattern. | Maya
C-2026-114 | FinFlow | Gold | us-west1 | 80 | 64 | 82% | 2026-07-20 -> 2026-10-19 | 8 | New customer; commercial offered seasonal boost. Soft pin recommended (can fall back to vram-quantized variant). | Priya
C-2025-310 | AtlasMaps | Silver | eu-central1 | 40 | 36 | 68% | rolling monthly | 2 | Long-tail nightly batch loads; low latency tolerance for tiles serving. | Liam
C-2026-208 | BeaconRetail | Enterprise | us-east1 | 200 | 200 | 91% | 2026-07-01 -> 2027-06-30 | 20 | Contractually reserved; operationally high p90 usage. Must maintain full slice unless SRE approves overflow to dedicated-burst. | Diego
C-2026-220 | NovaChat | Bronze | asia-east1 | 16 | 12 | 45% | 2026-08-01 -> 2026-11-01 | 0 | Low-priority; candidate for transient spill to hosted pool during daytime. | Rina
C-2026-233 | LumenAI | Gold | us-west1 | 48 | 36 | 88% | 2026-07-10 -> 2026-12-31 | 5 | Overlap with StellarHealth and FinFlow in week-of-07-15. Suggested burst schedule: Lumen off-peak eviction window 02:00-06:00 PT. | Maya

AGGREGATE REGION SITUATION (us-west1):
- Total slices reserved (contracts): 248
- Provisional allocations (after buffer & tiling): 204
- Physical pool available: 210 slices
- Headroom: +6 slices (fragile: depends on not exceeding p90 projected peaks).
- Risk: 3 overlapping Enterprise/Gold claims in key marketing weeks (07-15 to 08-01) could exceed physical capacity by ~18 slices if p90 realized.

TILING SCENARIOS (applied when physical < provisional demand):
1) Conservative (preserve contractual reservation): enforce contractual slices; enable temporary cross-region failover (customer pays data transfer).
- Expected utilization: +2% latency SLA breaches, retention of revenue.
2) Balanced (preferred): apply fairshare tiling per SLA weight, reduce provisional allocations by up to 15% for non-Enterprise customers, and schedule deterministic eviction windows for Gold/Bronze during defined surge windows.
- Expected utilization: +6% throughput efficiency; 1–2% lower latency under heavy concurrent peaks.
3) Aggressive (utilization-first): compress Silver/Bronze to quantized model variants and share across burst pools; only Enterprise guaranteed.
- Expected utilization: +12% capacity headroom; higher commercial risk.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION PLAYBOOK (Concierge steps):
1) Detect overlap via daily reconciliation job (recon runs 03:00 UTC). Flag contracts with shared region/time overlapping >7 days.
2) Triage: run 'impact score' (SLA weight * projected p90 shortfall).
3) Owner outreach: Capacity Concierge pings customer success + account owner + technical contact with 'expected impact' template.
4) Temporary plan: propose one of the TILING SCENARIOS and a fallback (e.g., quantized variant, cross-region failover). Shared doc and 48-hour SLA for response.
5) If no response, escalate to Sales Ops for commercial hold; implement Balanced tiling after 72 hours.

OPERATIONAL NOTES / FORMULAS USED (human-readable):
- provisional_allocation = max( reserved_slices - floor(buffer), min(reserved_slices, floor(physical_pool * (contract_share_weight))) )
- contract_share_weight = (SLA_weight * committed_dollars) / sum_over_region(SLA_weight * committed_dollars)
- buffer calculation follows policy per SLA tier above.

OPEN QUESTIONS (items for infra sync):
- Do we want to default cross-region failover to same-OR-net (cheaper transfer) or require explicit customer opt-in? (owner: Maya)
- Can Sales accept a one-time invoice credit for a forced downgrade to quantized variant during a capacity emergency? (owner: Priya)
- Should we automate a 24-hour hold/start timer when commercial approves a surge? (owner: Diego)

ACTIONS (next steps):
- Maya: collect proof-of-burst (last 6 months) from StellarHealth by 2026-07-22.
- Priya: confirm commercial fallback language for new Gold contracts in template by 2026-07-26.
- Liam: add us-west1 'surge window' to the daily recon job and publish runbook patch (INF-RUN-24) by 2026-07-23.

REFERENCES & LINKS:
- Slack thread: #capacity-concierge (link pinned in Confluence page)
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Capacity+Tiling+Playbook
- Reconciliation job: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/recon-daily

NOTES TO SELF (working):
- This sheet will be the input into reservation-allocator service (to be instrumented with canary deploy). Keep changes deliberate; mark final allocations with 'approved-by' column when signed off.
- Consider adding a per-customer historical elasticity score to inform tiling decisions (longer term).

END OF WORKING SHEET.
